Point & Click Solutions is seeking a Software Developer to build and maintain healthcare applications used by clinical and administrative teams. You will work across modern  ASP.NET Core applications, established .NET systems, SQL Server databases, and patient-facing web experiences.
Responsibilities
Develop and maintain applications using C#, ASP.NET Core, Razor, JavaScript, and SQL Server.
Design APIs, services, background jobs, database procedures, and responsive user interfaces.
Troubleshoot issues across application, database, integration, and deployment layers.
Write automated unit and browser-based integration tests.
Modernize legacy .NET and Windows components while preserving production reliability.
Build secure integrations using REST, SOAP, SFTP, XML, and healthcare data formats.
Participate in code reviews, technical design, testing, and release validation.
Protect sensitive healthcare data through secure coding and authorization practices.
Collaborate with product, support, QA, and implementation teams to translate operational needs into practical solutions.
Required Qualifications
Professional experience with C# and .NET.
Experience developing web applications with ASP.NET Core or ASP.NET MVC.
Strong SQL Server and T-SQL skills, including stored procedures and query optimization.
Working knowledge of HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and common web development patterns.
Experience with Git, automated testing, debugging, and code review.
Ability to understand and improve an established, business-critical codebase.
Clear written and verbal communication skills.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with Dapper, Razor, jQuery, Bootstrap, or Entity Framework Core.
Experience with xUnit, NUnit, Playwright, or similar testing tools.
Familiarity with Quartz.NET , SignalR, OpenID Connect, IIS, and Windows services.
Experience modernizing legacy .NET Framework, VB.NET , COM, or desktop applications.
Knowledge of CI/CD pipelines, Gulp, Jenkins, Swagger/OpenAPI, or NLog.
Experience with healthcare software, HIPAA-sensitive data, patient portals, billing, scheduling, or clinical workflows.
Familiarity with multi-tenant applications and security-based data partitioning.
What Success Looks Like
A successful developer will produce clear, maintainable solutions; investigate problems across the full stack; balance modernization with compatibility; and steadily improve the reliability and usability of software that supports healthcare delivery.
